public_sources.title: Calibrate What You SHIP: Post-Selection Risk Control for Verifier-Guided Text-to-Image Generation
public_sources.relevance: Candidate-level verifier calibration can fail after search/selection; the complete deployed selection/release policy must be calibrated on held-out inputs. The paper reports GenEval2 FLUX N=16 pooled-candidate released risk 0.310 versus 0.162 under policy-level SHIP calibration.

public_sources.relevance: Conditional e-variable factors may be chosen using past information and multiplied under optional continuation when each next factor is conditionally e-valid.

main_result.title: An inexact verify-before-reveal firewall must budget policy-level harmful acceptance, not raw verifier mismatch. Exact preservation of the evaluation sufficient statistic is the preferred contract when available.

harmful_accept_theorem.statement: For evaluation/release j, let H_j be the event that the fast path is revealed even though it differs from the frozen canonical attempt in the decision-relevant sufficient statistic used by the downstream test. If before reveal the full policy is frozen and P(H_j | past)<=v_j with pathwise sum_j v_j<=V_verify, and the downstream evaluation has false-commit probability <=A_eval conditional on no H_j, then P(any false commit)<=V_verify+A_eval. If the statistical certification of the verifier contract itself can be wrong with probability A_vcert, add A_vcert. No independence across uses is required.
harmful_accept_theorem.key_change: The verifier target should be harmful statistic discrepancy, not necessarily full-output inequality. Exact output equality is sufficient but may be over-strict; exact statistic-preservation is also sufficient for the evaluation test and can admit harmless output differences without spending V_verify.
harmful_accept_theorem.generation_rule: Any model/runtime/hardware/verifier-code/version change creates a new verifier generation. Do not carry a probabilistic v_j contract or an exact-statistic contract silently across a generation boundary.

selection_amplification.counterexample: If K candidates are searched and a harmful candidate is released whenever any candidate-level verifier false-accepts, independent 1% candidate-level false accepts give policy-level false-accept probability 1-(0.99)^K. At K=16 this is 0.14854; without independence the union-bound upper bound is 0.16.
selection_amplification.policy_calibration_rule: Calibrate or certify the complete scheduler/search/verifier/release policy on held-out inputs. Candidate-level FPR/FNR is not a deployment-risk certificate once the policy selects, routes, retries, or stops using verifier outputs.
selection_amplification.connection_to_SHIP: SHIP directly demonstrates this candidate-to-policy estimand shift under verifier-guided search; its N=16 example reports pooled-candidate released risk 0.310 versus 0.162 after policy-level calibration.

lifetime_budget_stress.formula: With zero harmful false accepts in n iid held-out policy executions, the one-sided exact upper bound p_u solving (1-p_u)^n=delta is p_u=1-delta^(1/n). The table inverts this for delta=.05 and .005. These are calibration-scale stresses, not live-system measurements.
lifetime_budget_stress.search_opportunity_stress: For M=1000 lifetime releases, K=16 verifier-guided candidate opportunities per release, and only the worst-case union bound, a uniform candidate-opportunity budget is V_verify/(M*K)=3.125e-7. Zero failures would require about 16,954,613 candidate opportunities to certify that level at 99.5% confidence.
lifetime_budget_stress.enriched_harmful_case_route: If an externally justified upper bound says harmful mismatch prevalence <=1%, then for M=1000 the verifier conditional miss rate on harmful mismatches may be as high as 5e-4 while keeping per-release harmful-accept risk <=5e-6. Zero misses among 10,594 representative harmful cases certifies miss rate <=5e-4 at 99.5% confidence. This shortcut is valid only if the challenge distribution covers/dominates live harmful discrepancies; enrichment alone is not a deployment guarantee.

correlated_verifier_warning.statement: Repeating inexact verifiers and accepting only unanimous passes does not generally multiply error probabilities. In a simple common-blind-spot model with per-check independent miss e=.01 outside a shared failure mode of probability c, k unanimous checks miss with probability c+(1-c)e^k.
correlated_verifier_warning.empirical_relevance: JuryProbe observes substantial shared false-negative structure in reference-free LLM judge panels; therefore independence must be demonstrated, not inferred from model diversity or repeated calls.

path_hierarchy.cost_role: Baseline decision-critical path when no stronger fast-path contract exists.

path_hierarchy.soundness: V_verify=0 inside frozen deterministic verifier scope.
path_hierarchy.cost_role: Rollback/verification overhead only; may reject harmless output differences.

path_hierarchy.soundness: V_verify=0 if the verifier exactly proves equality of the downstream evaluation sufficient statistic.
path_hierarchy.cost_role: Potentially lower rollback than exact-output checking because harmless textual/token differences may be accepted. This is a design candidate, not a measured systems result.

path_hierarchy.soundness: Requires lifetime V_verify ledger, policy-level harmful-accept calibration/certification, frozen verifier generation, and fail-closed behavior on uncertainty.
path_hierarchy.cost_role: Can reduce verification cost but statistical certification becomes expensive at long lifetime horizons.

path_hierarchy.soundness: Requires A_cert+A_eval+D_lease accounting from the prior checkpoint.
path_hierarchy.cost_role: Avoids per-output verification but pays large calibration and prospective drift assumptions.

lease_vs_per_output_verification_break_e.source_K: Prior worker-local admission stress used K=2276 calibration pairs for the first statistical lease.
lease_vs_per_output_verification_break_e.formula: If exact per-output verification adds g canonical-cost units per live evaluation while a statistical lease costs K upfront, the lease needs L>K/g evaluations merely to amortize calibration before considering monitoring or drift.
lease_vs_per_output_verification_break_e.comparison_to_prior_risk_horizon: The prior checkpoint's optimistic drift stress with d=.005 and h=1e-6 allowed only L_max=5012 evaluations. Under that stress, a per-output verifier costing <=~0.454 canonical units is cheaper than the statistical lease before the drift budget expires. This is an analytic comparison using worker-local synthetic quantities, not an observed serving cost.

new_measurement_validity_rules: Define verifier failure on the decision-relevant sufficient statistic, not raw output difference, unless exact output equality is itself the required property.

A verifier-guided search/selection system must be calibrated as the complete deployed policy. Per-candidate verifier error rates do not automatically control released-output or committed-evidence risk.
Use a non-resetting lifetime V_verify ledger over harmful accepted mismatches. Re-certification or verifier replacement does not reset lifetime risk.
Do not exponentiate verifier reliability across repeated or multi-judge checks without a justified conditional-independence contract. Shared blind spots impose an error floor.

Statistical challenge-set certification may reduce sample cost only when coverage of live harmful discrepancies is justified; zero failures on a narrow synthetic family is not a universal verifier certificate.
False rejects/abstentions of a fail-closed verifier are primarily cost/coverage events; false accepts are soundness events and must be separated in reporting.
When exact statistic-preserving verification is available, compare it against exact-output checking because it can preserve test validity while avoiding rollback on harmless output differences.
scope_guards: All sample-size and break-even tables are analytic/worker-local stress calculations, not measurements of any production evaluator, serving stack, verifier, or drift process.
The harmful-accept theorem assumes the downstream evaluation remains valid conditional on no harmful verifier acceptance; it does not repair a flawed downstream test.
SHIP is a text-to-image release-calibration result. Its exact numbers do not transfer to LLM evaluation; its supported general lesson here is the candidate-to-policy calibration mismatch.

JuryProbe provides an empirical dependence diagnostic, not a formal risk guarantee. Its observed correlations/lifts show why independence cannot be assumed but do not quantify a different verifier panel without new calibration.

Exact statistic-preserving verification can set V_verify=0 only if equality of the test-relevant statistic is truly exact within the frozen scope. Approximate semantic equivalence must remain in the probabilistic path.

frontier.action: Derive a statistic-preserving verifier for the paired evaluation setting itself: identify the minimal sufficient statistic whose exact equality is enough to preserve the e-process/McNemar decision, and compare rollback frequency theoretically with full-output equality.

Build a policy-level held-out certification protocol for probabilistic verify-before-reveal using complete hedging/search trajectories, simultaneous threshold control, and a non-resetting V_verify budget. Stress verifier-guided selection, retry, and stop policies rather than isolated candidate checks.

Quantify common-mode verifier failure under heterogeneous panels and grounded/canonical fallback. Compare unanimous inexact panels with one exact/grounded verifier under matched compute; do not assume independence.

Optimize lifetime V_verify allocation across common/rare fingerprints and time: compare equal, 1/[j(j+1)], and value-weighted predictable allocations while preserving policy-level calibration and verifier-generation invalidation.

Stress verifier drift explicitly: freeze a policy-level calibration, then change task mix/model/runtime/verifier version and measure how quickly harmful-accept risk exceeds its certificate; compare scheduled recalibration with exact statistic verification.

exact_next_action: Construct the minimal statistic-preserving verifier for paired binary evaluation: prove which canonical quantities must match for the downstream sign/e-process to be pathwise identical, then quantify how much exact-output checking over-verifies. In parallel, formalize a SHIP-style full-policy held-out certificate for the probabilistic fallback.
